gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long these devices actually lasted in a named reviewer's test: OutdoorGearLab measured the Fitbit Charge 6 at just under 7 days and about 8 h of GPS, and the Garmin vívoactive 6 at about 11 days (about 5 with always-on screen) and 20 h of GPS. Geek Culture's Apple Watch Series 11 lasted about 32 h with always-on display, sleep tracking and a 2 h workout.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Apple Series 11 tech specs (support.apple.com/en-mide/125093), which give only Apple's 24 h and 38 h low-power ratings and Apple's own test script. The other cited page, Google's Charge 6 specs, did not render for me. The top results add no measurements either: sekin.in repeats maker ratings and Google's accuracy claims. androidcentral.com/best-fitbit lists the Charge 6 as '7 days; 5 hours (GPS)' with no tester figure for it. nymag would not load. None of them gives a measured runtime or a heart-rate check against a chest strap for these models.
decides: It confirms the tracker-vs-watch split ChatGPT gave, but the measured gap is smaller than the ratings suggest. Measured, the Series 11 ran about 32 h against the Charge 6's roughly 7 days, so about 5x, not 7x. Measured runtimes also make the Garmin vívoactive 6 the in-between pick: about 11 days like a band, plus 20 h of GPS, which beats the band's roughly 8 h. That suits a buyer who wants smartwatch features without charging daily. Heart-rate checks show the Charge 6 is not a compromise for steady workouts: OutdoorGearLab measured it within ±3 bpm of a Polar H10, and Notebookcheck found about 1% deviation.
